newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico says eight groups vying for natgas licence.
newsitem.headline: Mexico says eight groups vying for natgas licence.

text.p: Mexico's Energy Ministry said Sunday eight consortia had expressed interest in the upcoming auction for a licence to distribute natural gas in the Tampico, Ciudad Madero and Altamira zone.

The ministry said it estimated the development of the natural gas distribution in the zone, which lies on the Gulf of Mexico, would need an investment of more than $40 million and would have a minimum of 25,000 clients inside 5 years.

The interested groups are Bufete Industrial; Repsol Mexico SA, a unit of Spain's Repsol SA ; a consortium made up of Grupo Mexicano de Desarrollo, B.C. Gas Inc. and Shell Oil Company; Compania Mexicana de Gas SA; France's G.D.F. International; NorAm Energy de Mexico and Corporacion Gutsa; U.S.-based KN Energy Inc. and Southern Union Energy International; and Mexico's Servicios Industriales Administrativos SA.
The ministry said the auction result will be announced Sept. 11 at the latest.
Mexico is auctioning off licences to distribute natural gas on a zone by zone basis.
